title: Commit adds a node_modules symlink to an absolute host path
detail: 7d9bd9a adds node_modules as a symlink (mode 120000) to /home/claude/danizee-claude-suite/node_modules; .gitignore only ignores node_modules/ so the link got through; dangling in every other clone and exposes the host path
fix_hint: git rm --cached node_modules; ignore node_modules without the trailing slash

title: An untracked path git cannot diff exits 1 and is dropped silently, so a failure can become 'no change to review'
detail: git diff --no-index exits 1 both for differences and for some errors (an untracked nested repo: error Could not access 'sub/null', exit 1, empty stdout); only code>1 is a failure, so diff-range exits 3 and --json lists the path under untracked with empty:true
fix_hint: treat code 1 with empty stdout or non-empty stderr as a failure; list a path in untracked only when its diff text is non-empty

title: Command text still says any non-zero exit is a failure although the blocks exit 3 for an empty range
detail: the graph paragraph never mentions exit 3 and says a non-zero exit is a broken state; the lens and impact paragraphs say the same right after the exit-3 sentence; same text in the regenerated w-review.md
fix_hint: say 'any non-zero exit other than 3 (empty range)' in all three paragraphs and add the exit-3 sentence to the graph paragraph

title: The impact block calls diff-range twice and the --base advice covers only one call
detail: the diff and the base-only call can be given different bases and nothing notices
fix_hint: resolve the base once into B and pass --base $B to both diff-range and impact, or say the ref goes on both calls

title: Non-UTF-8 file content is rewritten as U+FFFD in the printed diff
detail: defaultGit decodes stdout as utf-8, so a latin-1 byte becomes EF BF BD and the diff no longer matches the file
fix_hint: read the diff calls' stdout as a Buffer and let raw be a Buffer that cli.js writes undecoded

title: An untracked symlink to a directory makes the whole verb exit 1
detail: git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <link> follows a symlink to a directory and fails exit 1 with 'Could not access <link>/null'; the exit-1-with-stderr rule then throws, so lenses, graph and impact all stop with diff-range failed; a .gitignore line node_modules/ does not match a worktree's node_modules link (reproduced on git 2.43)
fix_hint: lstat each untracked path first; for a symlink build the added-file diff from the link target text (mode 120000) instead of following it; add a test with a symlink to a directory

title: When the merge base fails with an upstream set, the range silently becomes the whole history
detail: when @{upstream} resolves but merge-base fails (exit 1 in a shallow clone, or 128), the code falls through to the empty tree with no error, so every tracked file is reported as the change (reproduced with a --depth 1 clone)
fix_hint: with an upstream and no merge base, exit 1 with 'no merge base with <upstream> (shallow clone?): pass --base'; keep the empty-tree fallback only for no upstream

title: --base refuses the empty-tree id that --base-only prints in a SHA-256 repository
detail: --base-only prints hash-object -t tree /dev/null (6ef19b41... in a sha256 repo) but --base accepts only the hard-coded SHA-1 constant, so the w-review blast-radius block always fails there (reproduced with git init --object-format=sha256)
fix_hint: compare f.base with the repository's own hash-object -t tree /dev/null result instead of the SHA-1 constant

title: The blast-radius block ignores a failed --base-only and reports a misleading second error
detail: nothing checks the first call's exit status; when it fails B is empty and the second call fails with '--base needs a ref', which misleads the diagnosis (nothing is skipped: the step still exits non-zero)
fix_hint: test [ -n "$B" ] (or || { echo 'diff-range --base-only failed' >&2; (exit 1); }) before the second call

title: Any stderr warning on an untracked-file diff aborts the whole range (core.autocrlf / eol=crlf)
detail: exit 1 with any stderr text is treated as failure; with core.autocrlf=true git prints a benign 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' warning for every LF text file while the diff on stdout is correct (confirmed on git 2.43), so every untracked text file fails the range on those setups
fix_hint: run the --no-index diff with -c core.safecrlf=false, or treat only stderr lines not starting with 'warning:' as failure; add a test with core.autocrlf=true

title: Hand-written symlink diff header does not quote paths as git does; a newline in the name injects diff lines
detail: the symlink block writes the raw name in 'diff --git' and '+++' lines; git C-quotes names with quotes, backslashes, control chars or newlines (and non-ASCII under core.quotePath) and adds a TAB after a name with a space; a symlink named with an embedded newline split the header and parseDiff read a path that does not exist
fix_hint: quote the name as git does (C-style quoting, TAB after ---/+++ names with a space), or skip-and-report an untracked symlink whose name has a newline; add tests with a space, a quote and a newline

title: diff-range runs programs and can fetch over the network when the reviewed repo's .git/config says so (textconv, clean filters, fsmonitor, lazy fetch)
detail: defaultGit only sets core.hooksPath=/dev/null and strips GIT_*; a planted .git/config with diff.X.textconv, filter.X.clean and core.fsmonitor ran all three programs during diff-range (markers created), textconv output replaced the real content the lenses read, and a blob:none partial clone fetched missing blobs from the promisor remote with the user's credential helper; the header claims a hardened read
fix_hint: apply safe-git's overrides to both diff calls: --no-textconv, -c core.fsmonitor= -c diff.external= -c credential.helper= -c protocol.allow=never and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 in env (a missing blob then exits 1 with a clear message); state the remaining trust assumption in the header

title: --ignore-submodules=all makes a committed submodule pointer bump disappear (exit 3)
detail: a superproject pointer bump with --base HEAD~1 prints nothing and exits 3; with a hostile submodule config, --ignore-submodules=dirty printed the pointer change and ran no program, while none ran the submodule's clean filter
fix_hint: use --ignore-submodules=dirty on both diffs (the flag overrides diff.ignoreSubmodules=all); test a pointer bump in range with a planted filter not running; update the header

title: An include.path in the untrusted repo's config is followed with no timeout: a FIFO hangs the verb forever
detail: mkfifo .git/inc + git config include.path inc made git config -z --list block forever; defaultGit uses spawnSync with no timeout; safe-git uses --no-includes and a timeout on every child
fix_hint: pass a timeout to every git child and exit 1 on expiry with a plain message, and/or read the config with --no-includes (then includes are data not followed); name the remaining gap in the header

title: Many driver names overflow GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS: E2BIG with a jargon error
detail: 600 filter sections make spawnSync fail with E2BIG (128 KiB single env string cap); it fails closed but the message says nothing useful
fix_hint: put per-driver pairs on argv as -c options (as safe-git does) and keep only the statics in the env, or exit 1 with 'too many filter/diff/merge drivers configured (N) to switch off safely'

title: Partial-clone error text is nested and jargon-heavy with no runnable next step
detail: the message nests parentheses two deep and uses promisor/GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH/transports without a command
fix_hint: one plain sentence with a command: this is a partial clone and some file contents are not downloaded; diff-range never downloads; run git -C <dir> diff <base> >/dev/null once, or use a full clone

title: No test checks that every git call carries the hardened env or that an inherited GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is replaced
detail: the planted-config test proves the programs do not run during the diffs but no test records the env per call; a future call through the unwrapped runner would pass the suite
fix_hint: add a recording fake around defaultGit asserting every call's env has the overrides, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1, and that a caller's GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is dropped

title: Include refusal reads only --local, so an include in the per-worktree config (config.worktree) is followed and its filter driver runs
detail: with extensions.worktreeConfig=true git also reads $GIT_DIR/config.worktree, which --local does not cover; a filter defined in a file included from config.worktree is never found by the --no-includes driver read but the diffs follow the include (reproduced: PWNED created, exit 0); the header claims nothing named in any config git reads is executed
fix_hint: read git config --list -z --no-includes --show-scope once and refuse include.path/includeIf.*.path in scope local or worktree; add a test with a config.worktree include

title: Header says nothing from any config git reads is executed, but drivers defined in files the user's global/system config includes are not switched off
detail: the driver list comes from --no-includes, the diffs follow global includes; the header contradicts itself
fix_hint: narrow the sentence: drivers defined in files your own global/system config includes are yours and are not switched off

title: Any signal death is reported as a timeout
detail: with a timeout set, r.signal && !r.error turns any signal (OOM SIGKILL, SIGPIPE, external kill) into the 'took longer than N ms' message
fix_hint: use the timeout message only for r.error?.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'; report other signals as 'git <cmd> was killed by <signal>'

title: Partial-clone note asserts 'this is a partial clone' on any matching error and its command is not runnable for paths with spaces
detail: the MISSING regex also matches a corrupt full clone's 'bad object'/'unable to read'; the suggested git -C ${dir} is unquoted
fix_hint: say 'if this is a partial clone' (or check remote.*.promisor / extensions.partialClone) and single-quote the dir

title: /w-review does not name the refused case (exit 2) diff-range can now return
detail: exit 2 is reachable (an include in the repo config, a bad driver name) but the text says any other non-zero exit is wrong input or a broken state
fix_hint: append: exit 2 means diff-range refused the repository (e.g. an include in its own config): report the refusal as printed; regenerate w-review.md

title: Include refusal message gives an unclear remedy
detail: 'run the read through safe-git' names no command and safe-git does not produce this range
fix_hint: say: remove the include from .git/config (git config --local --unset include.path) and run diff-range again

title: One hardened git process per untracked file, with no cap and no overall time bound
detail: 2,000 one-line untracked files took 8.4 s (4.2 ms each); 50,000 would take minutes, w-review runs it three times, --timeout bounds each child only, no --max-untracked and no count in the output
fix_hint: diff all untracked files in one process: temp GIT_INDEX_FILE copy, git add -N -- <files> with the same overrides, one git diff <base>; or cap the count, list the rest in skipped and print a note

title: Output over 64 MiB fails with an unnamed ENOBUFS, and no size cap matches downstream's 32 MiB limit
detail: a 70 MB untracked log gives 'kit: cannot run git: spawnSync git ENOBUFS' with no path or remedy; a 50 MB range passes diff-range but graph/impact refuse it (maxDiffBytes 32 MiB); the range is held three times in memory
fix_hint: map ENOBUFS to a message naming the command, output size and (in diff-range) the untracked path; lstat untracked files and put any above a byte cap in skipped with reason too_large; refuse a total above graph's maxDiffBytes with a clear message

title: Header and a test title still say the partial-clone failure names that lazy fetch is off
detail: the message now says diff-range never downloads; the header line and the test title at test/kit-diff-range.test.js:370 still claim the lazy-fetch wording
fix_hint: change both to 'naming the missing object and that diff-range never downloads'

title: Merged add -N diff pairs a deleted tracked file with an untracked copy as a rename, so the content disappears
detail: a tracked old.txt moved by hand to untracked new.txt printed only rename from/to with no hunks; the --no-index fallback printed a delete plus a full add; the two paths differ and lenses/graph see no content
fix_hint: add --no-renames to the diff (both paths) so an intent-to-add file is always a new-file entry; test both paths on a hand-moved file

title: In a sparse checkout an untracked file outside the cone makes the whole verb exit 1
detail: git add -N refuses paths outside the sparse-checkout definition; that stderr does not match the fallback regex, so the verb exits 1 with a mislabelled 'cannot list the untracked files' error; the fallback works
fix_hint: pass --sparse to add -N (an older git without it already takes the fallback) and relabel the error 'cannot add the untracked files to the temporary index'

title: A range whose only changes were skipped by the caps exits 3, which w-review reports as no change to review
detail: a repo whose only change is a 9 MB new file exits 3 with only a stderr note; same with --max-untracked 0; the header's own rule says an unread untracked path is never exit 3
fix_hint: when the diff is empty but skipped holds max_untracked or too_large entries, exit 1 naming the skipped files; test a single oversized new file

title: With core.splitIndex on, add -N on the temporary index writes a new sharedindex file into the real .git
detail: one run left a new .git/sharedindex.<sha>; the verb writes to a repository it claims only to read
fix_hint: run the add and the diff with -c core.splitIndex=false

title: An unconditional --sparse sends git 2.25-2.33 to the per-file fallback on every run
detail: git add --sparse shipped in 2.34; older gits reject it as unknown option and always take the --no-index loop; before 2.34 add -N ignores the cone anyway
fix_hint: pass --sparse only when the config read shows core.sparseCheckout=true, or retry add -N once without --sparse before the per-file fallback

title: Fallback regex matches any stderr that contains 'sparse' or 'usage:'
detail: a real add -N failure mentioning a path with 'sparse' quietly switches to the slow path and the real cause is never reported
fix_hint: anchor on git's option-parse failure only: /unknown (option|switch) `(sparse|pathspec-from-file|pathspec-file-nul)/ or exit 129 with usage:

title: Usage and header give exit 3 / exit 1 for empty and cap-only ranges, but --json exits 0 in both
detail: with --json no exit is returned; nothing names the --json exit code or says to read empty and skipped_detail; no test covers the cap-only --json case
fix_hint: add '(--json: always exit 0; read empty and skipped_detail)' to usage and header; add one assertion on the cap-only --json result

title: An unreadable untracked file fails the whole verb as 'cannot diff against the base'
detail: a mode-000 untracked file makes the merged diff exit 128 and the message points at the base, not the untracked file
fix_hint: label a failing merged diff 'cannot diff the range (tracked changes plus N untracked files)'

title: The --sparse retry never runs on a real git 2.25-2.33 because git's usage text lists --pathspec-from-file
detail: the retry requires !/pathspec-/ on the whole stderr, but git prints the full add usage after the error line and that usage names --pathspec-from-file; so the per-file fallback is taken instead; the tests fake stderr without the usage body
fix_hint: test only the first error:/fatal: line of stderr for both the sparse match and the pathspec exclusion; add a usage body with --pathspec-from-file to the fake stderr in the tests

title: When TMPDIR is unwritable the run fails with a bare EACCES although the per-file path needs no temp folder
detail: fs.mkdtemp is not wrapped; a read-only /tmp fails the verb as soon as any untracked file exists
fix_hint: catch the mkdtemp/copyFile failure and fall through to the per-file path, or raise a KitExit naming TMPDIR

title: The usage line describes --json too narrowly and says it always exits 0, which the code does not do
detail: skipped also holds too_large and max_untracked entries; under --json the code still exits 2 for an oversized range or a config include and 1 for failures
fix_hint: say skipped/skipped_detail cover nested repositories and cap-skipped files, and --json exits 0 whenever a summary is printed; errors and refusals keep 1/2

title: An unreadable real index is reported as a TMPDIR failure
detail: copyFile sits in the same try as mkdtemp, so an EACCES/EIO on .git/index prints 'cannot create a temporary index in <tmpdir>'; the per-file output is still correct
fix_hint: name the failing step in the note (create a temporary index / copy the index)

title: TMPDIR fallback test covers only mkdtemp ENOENT, not a copyFile failure or temp-dir cleanup
detail: no test makes mkdtemp succeed and copyFile fail and checks that no diff-range-index-* dir is left
fix_hint: add a case with a writable TMPDIR where the copy fails and assert no leftover temp dir

title: callers --symbol: exit 0 with a `missing` symbol or `partial: true` is not covered
detail: caller-floor.js run() returns exit 0 with NO entry for a symbol whose file was not read, whose name is not in the file, or whose path does not exist: the symbol goes to `missing` with a reason, and `partial`/`not_read` are set. The step never mentions `missing`, `partial` or `not_read`, so a symbol with no entry reads as 'no callers' on a normal input (typo, renamed file, unread or too-large file).
fix_hint: Add: 'Exit 0 can still leave a symbol out: read `missing` (each with its reason) and `partial`/`not_read`; a symbol in `missing` was not answered, never "no callers".'

title: Receipt is recorded before Compound and leaves out untracked files, so push-gate check will not match the reviewed change
detail: The receipt is keyed on sha256(base, tree); the tree is HEAD plus tracked changes only (status --untracked-files=no, add -u). The closing step runs before Compound, which writes docs/solutions/ideas/<name>.md, and the build's new files are usually still untracked. Once committed, the HEAD tree differs from the receipt tree and push-gate check asks or denies.
fix_hint: Say to stage new files (git add -N or git add) before the receipt and to re-record after Compound if it changes tracked files; or move the receipt after Compound. State that untracked files are not part of the receipt.

title: Exit 2 explained only for diff-range; the lenses, graph and impact refusals and the --base-only refusal are mislabeled
detail: graph and impact document exit 2 refused but the step names exit 2 only as a diff-range refusal; diff-range also refuses on a range over 32 MiB. In block 3 a refusal from diff-range --base-only prints 'base was not resolved' and forces RC=1, so the exit 2 is lost.
fix_hint: Name exit 2 for each verb as 'refused: report as printed', and in block 3 keep the --base-only exit code instead of forcing RC=1.

title: scrub --worktree does not scan the new untracked files that the build just created
detail: The text says 'tracked files' but reads exit 0 as clear to commit. New files from the TDD build are untracked until added, so a secret in a new file passes this step.
fix_hint: Tell the reader to git add -N the new files before scrub --worktree, or say untracked files were not scanned.

title: push-gate check exit codes not named
detail: The step tells the user to run push-gate check but not what its exits mean: 0 abstain or ask (read decision), 2 deny, 1 error. Exit 0 could be read as approved.
fix_hint: Add one sentence: exit 0 = abstain or ask (read decision), 2 = deny, 1 = error; none is an allow.

title: Other copies of the /w-plan-tdd-swarm description still say 9 phases
detail: The template now says all 12 phases, but src/utils/shortcuts.js:454 and WORKFLOW-SHORTCUTS.md:442 still say 'Use TodoWrite first with all 9 phases'.
fix_hint: Update both descriptions to 12 phases, or drop the count.

title: diff-range exit 0 with skipped files is read as a complete range
detail: diff-range exits 0 and still prints the diff when it has left untracked files out (too_large over 8 MiB, max_untracked over 20000 files, or a nested repository), writing a note to stderr and listing them in skipped_detail. Nothing tells the agent an exit-0 range can be missing files, so lenses/graph/impact run on an incomplete range and the agent can write 'nothing else is affected' about files never in the diff.
fix_hint: Add one sentence: on exit 0, read diff-range's stderr; any skipped file (too_large, max_untracked, nested repository) was not analysed, so name it and treat every result as a floor. Add a test assertion.

title: Exit-code paragraph contradicts itself on exit 2
detail: 'Any other non-zero exit is wrong input or a broken state: report it, never skip the step' covers exit 2, while a later sentence says exit 2 is a refusal: stop that step. Two instructions for one code.
fix_hint: Say 'Exit 1 is wrong input or a broken state: report it, never skip the step', and keep exit 2 in its own sentence.

title: Empty-range path ends the block with status 3
detail: When diff-range exits 3, each block prints 'no change to review' then ends with (exit $RC), so its status is 3; the Bash tool shows a non-zero status as an error although the prose says exit 3 is never a failure.
fix_hint: In the 3) branch set RC=0 after the echo, or say that status 3 from the block is expected.

title: Missing kit is reported as a diff-range failure
detail: The blocks never check that .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js exists; when missing, node exits 1 and the block prints 'diff-range failed (exit 1)', which the prose says to report as a broken state, conflicting with the advisory fallback. A failing mktemp is reported the same way.
fix_hint: Start each block with [ -f .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js ] || { echo "kit missing: skipped (advisory)"; exit 0; } in a form that does not kill the shell.

title: push-gate check exit 2 is not always a deny
detail: check also exits 2 through a KitExit when the receipt store is refused (a symlink at or inside the receipts folder). That is a refusal of the store, not a deny decision about the change.
fix_hint: Say 'exit 2 deny (read decision and reason) or a refused receipt store (kit: refused: on stderr)'.

title: Skipped-file instruction asks for names the block output does not show
detail: A nested repository is listed only in skipped_detail (--json only, and none of the blocks passes --json; no stderr note). The max_untracked stderr note gives counts only, never names. An agent following the text literally must guess or drop the requirement.
fix_hint: Say that max_untracked prints only a count (report the count) and that nested repositories are visible only with diff-range --json (skipped_detail); or name each file only where stderr names it.

title: A failed mktemp is reported as 'diff-range failed (exit 1)'
detail: When mktemp is missing or TMPDIR unwritable, D is empty and the redirect fails before node runs; the block prints 'diff-range failed (exit 1)' although diff-range never ran. Fails closed, but the diagnosis names the wrong tool (all three blocks).
fix_hint: Guard the temp file: D=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$D" ] || { echo "mktemp failed: no temp file for the range" >&2; RC=1; } before calling diff-range.

title: Splitting the exit codes dropped the catch-all for codes other than 0-3
detail: The new text names only exits 0-3. A verb exit such as 127 or a signal (134/137) has no documented meaning for lenses, graph or impact.
fix_hint: Add: 'Any other non-zero exit (for example 127, or a signal) is a failure of that step: report it, never read it as nothing found.'

title: Range temp file is left behind if a block is interrupted
detail: The three Code Analysis blocks write the full diff-range output (which can include an untracked .env) to a mktemp file removed only by the trailing rm -f; no trap, so an interrupt during graph or impact leaves the copy in TMPDIR (mode 0600). Same pattern as the existing w-review blocks.
fix_hint: After mktemp succeeds add trap 'rm -f "$D"' EXIT INT TERM, or run the mktemp-to-rm part in a subshell with that trap.

title: Redact skipped in a linked worktree although the verb would find the secrets
detail: The block checks .claude/kit/secrets relative to the cwd and, if missing, writes the text as is. redact.js secretsRoots() looks in the worktree top and then the main checkout's .claude/kit/secrets (the file is git-ignored, so a linked worktree normally has no copy). Streams run in linked worktrees, so on that path the raw diff, with any real secrets, goes into the solution doc or memory export, which Phase 2 commits. Same when the cwd is a subdirectory.
fix_hint: Drop the shell existence check and always run redact --keep-lines when the kit is installed (with no secrets file the verb returns replaced 0), or check the same roots the verb checks.

title: A git diff failure in the redact pipeline is read as an empty, clean result
detail: In `git diff HEAD~1 | node ... redact --keep-lines; RC=$?`, RC is redact's exit only. If git diff fails, redact reads empty stdin and exits 0 with text ''. Reproduced with HEAD~5 on a 2-commit repo. The block also fixes the input to git diff HEAD~1 although the prose says any excerpt.
fix_hint: Write the diff to a temp file first and check git's exit code, then redact --keep-lines < file; or pipefail in a subshell and report PIPESTATUS.

title: 'abstain (no receipt)' is wrong: with no receipt, push-gate check returns ask
detail: push-gate.js decide(): a change with no receipt goes to block(), which returns ask at threshold none and deny at any other threshold, reason 'no review recorded for this change; run /w-review before pushing'. Abstain only comes from a passing receipt or an incomplete one that found nothing blocking. So every /bcp without a prior /w-review lands on ask and does not push, which contradicts the stream spec (no receipt → the push goes on) and would make the gate blocking. test/w-background-compound-command.test.js:74 asserts the wrong wording.
fix_hint: Say abstain = a passing or incomplete-but-clean receipt; state that no receipt returns ask with reason 'no review recorded…' (threshold none) or deny (stricter --threshold); for that one ask reason the push goes on and the summary says 'no review recorded, pushed'; any other ask is not pushed.

title: The background agent has no way to put an ask to the owner
detail: Phase 3 runs inside the autonomous background agent. On ask it is told to put the question to the owner, but a background agent cannot hold a conversation with the owner and nothing tells the lead to relay the ask or resume the push.
fix_hint: On ask, the agent stops and puts the gate's reason in the Phase 4 summary as 'not pushed — gate asks: <reason>'; the lead relays that to the owner and runs the push in the foreground only after they answer.

title: The merge-to-main push is not covered by the gate decision
detail: The gate checks the current branch's HEAD tree against its upstream merge-base. The step then merges into main and pushes main, a different change that is never checked.
fix_hint: Run push-gate check again on main after the merge and before pushing main, or state that the gate covers only the branch push.

title: A refused lead commit leaves the handoff files staged, and the agent's commit is not path-limited
detail: On a refused lead scrub the handoff files stay staged and dispatch still happens; Phase 2 'Commit with descriptive message' names no pathspec, so the lead's staged files would go into the agent's commit. Phase 2 exit 1 and other exits do not say 'skip Phase 3'.
fix_hint: Agent commits with git commit -- <its paths>. After a refused lead scrub: unstage and do not dispatch, or dispatch without --push. Add 'skip Phase 3' to Phase 2's exit 1 and other-exit clauses.

title: No test runs a block with the kit installed, and one temp dir leaks
detail: Tests only match wording and run blocks with no kit present; nothing runs push-gate check, scrub --worktree or the redact pipeline against a real repo. nodeMk() creates a temp dir never removed; an import sits mid-file.
fix_hint: Add a fixture repo with the kit copied in and assert the real decision, exit code and redacted text for each block. Remove the temp dir in finally; move the import to the top.

title: Redact block diffs the lead's handoff commit, not the session's work
detail: CHECKPOINT 1 commits the handoff files before the agent is dispatched, so the agent's `git diff HEAD~1` covers the handoff commit plus uncommitted edits, not the session's committed work. After a refused handoff scrub there is no handoff commit and the same line gives a different range. The real diff never goes through redact unless the agent improvises.
fix_hint: Have the lead record the pre-handoff HEAD (or the session's base) and pass it to the agent; diff that range in the block (git diff "$BASE"), never HEAD~1.

title: After a refused handoff scrub, the agent's scrub refuses too, so the claimed write-up commit never happens
detail: scrub --worktree scans every tracked file on disk. Unstaging only helps for a new file; a hit in an already-tracked handoff file stays on disk, the agent's Phase 2 scrub exits 2 and it does not commit, although the text promises the write-up commits.
fix_hint: Say the agent's scrub will also refuse while a tracked file holds the hit, or have the lead pass that fact so the agent skips Phase 2 and reports it. Do not claim the write-up commits.

title: Main re-check after the merge stops every reviewed change
detail: push-gate changeId hashes (merge-base with @{upstream}, HEAD tree). On main after the merge the base differs from the one the receipt was keyed on, so with any receipt decide() returns ask 'only an earlier review exists, for a different version of this change', which is not the no-review reason: a reviewed change is held while an unreviewed one goes through.
fix_hint: Have the main re-check pass --base set to the base the branch check used so a fast-forward merge of the reviewed tree matches its receipt; or document the outcome and route it to the relay explicitly.

title: Relay path loops: the lead's foreground rerun of Phase 3 stops on the same ask or deny
detail: After the owner answers, the lead runs the Phase 3 lines, push-gate block first; nothing changed, so the gate returns the same ask or deny and Phase 3 says not pushed. Read literally the owner's answer never leads to a push, and a deny is treated like an ask.
fix_hint: State that after the owner explicitly says go on an ask, the lead pushes without rerunning the gate's stop rule (the permission prompt still applies); a deny is never pushed past, the owner must fix the cause first.

title: Agent dispatched without --push after a handoff scrub refusal writes the wrong 'not pushed' reason
detail: The lead's text says the summary reads 'not pushed — handoff scrub refused', but the agent is dispatched without --push and Phase 3 writes 'not pushed — owner's go needed (/bcp)', misleading when the owner ran /bcp.
fix_hint: Have the lead put the reason into the agent's dispatch prompt, or write the line itself; make clear which.

title: MB is recorded after the branch push, so the main re-check never matches the branch's receipt
detail: The text pushes the branch first, then sets MB=$(git merge-base @{upstream} HEAD). A successful push moves the remote-tracking ref, so MB is HEAD, not the base the branch check used. push-gate check --base "$MB" on main then hashes a different id and returns ask 'only an earlier review exists…' even on a fast-forward. The no-upstream path mismatches too (branch check base null, main check resolves main's upstream).
fix_hint: Record MB right after the branch gate check, before pushing, and reuse it; for a branch with no upstream say the main check will ask, or reuse the branch check's base.

title: git restore --staged does not exist before git 2.23; a failed unstage leaves secret-bearing paths staged
detail: restore was added in git 2.23; on older git it fails with 'not a git command' and nothing checks the exit, so the paths holding the scrub hit stay staged and the user's next plain git commit would commit them.
fix_hint: Use git reset -q -- <paths>, which works on every git, or fall back to it when restore fails, and report a non-zero exit.

title: A branch push that fails still leads to the merge into main, the main push and the clean-up
detail: Nothing checks the branch push's exit status. Offline or rejected, the agent goes on to merge into local main, run the main gate, attempt the main push and clean up the branch, and the summary has no failed-push wording.
fix_hint: After a non-zero exit from the branch push stop Phase 3 (no merge, no main push, no clean-up) and write 'not pushed — push failed (exit N): <stderr>' into the summary; same for a failed main push.

title: 'The temp file is removed on every path' is not true when the shell is killed
detail: The redact block has a trailing rm -f and no trap; killed by a tool timeout, the full unredacted diff stays in TMPDIR.
fix_hint: Add trap 'rm -f "$D"' EXIT INT TERM once D is set, or soften the claim to 'every path the block completes'.

title: Plain git diff "$BASE" can lazy-fetch over the network and hang on a credential prompt
detail: The redact block and Step 1's category detection run a bare git diff. In a partial or promisor clone git fetches missing blobs on demand (a network call that is neither a Pi Brain read nor the owner's push) and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT is unset, so the background agent can stop at a credential prompt. diff-range turns lazy fetch off; the block skips that protection.
fix_hint: Write the range with the hardened verb: node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js diff-range --base "$BASE" --no-untracked > "$D" (check its exit the same way, exit 3 = empty range), or at least prefix with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0.

title: Redact rule skips ralph-candidates.md and the commit message, both of which get committed and pushed
detail: The rule requires redaction only before the solution doc or a memory export. The RC-D/RC-F diagnostics built from the diff go into .claude/ralph-candidates.md and the descriptive commit message can quote diff text; both go into the Phase 2 commit without redact. The scrub checks only the scrub-pattern list, not the secrets file.
fix_hint: Extend the rule to every write and commit that carries diff text: solution doc, ralph-candidates.md, memory exports and the commit message; each takes only the redacted text.

title: BASE from the dispatch prompt is passed to git diff without checking it is a commit
detail: A value starting with -- would be parsed as an option (e.g. --output=/some/path) and could write outside the repository. The lead normally writes a sha, so this is hardening.
fix_hint: Check BASE with git rev-parse --verify -q "$BASE^{commit}" and use the resolved sha (or --end-of-options); on failure RC=1 with 'BASE is not a commit'.

title: MB is recorded but never printed or carried to the main re-check
detail: Phase 3 records MB before the branch push and uses it in the main check, but never echoes it or says to keep it; shell state does not carry between tool calls, so the main check runs with MB empty, push-gate falls back to main's upstream merge-base and every /bcp of a reviewed branch stops on a spurious 'only an earlier review exists' ask.
fix_hint: Record and print in one step (MB=$(...); echo "MB=$MB"); say the agent keeps that sha and sets MB=<sha> in the shell that runs the main check, and leaves out --base when it is empty.

title: Phase 1 Analyze/Append run before the redact block and name a different input
detail: Phase 1 lists 'Analyze: parse git diff' and the Append-to-ralph-candidates steps before the redact rule and block. Followed in order the agent analyses plain git diff (often nothing after the handoff commit), without diff-range's hardening, and writes RC-D/RC-F entries before redact has run.
fix_hint: Make the redact block the first Phase 1 step; reword Analyze to parse the redacted text the block printed (the range since $BASE) and Append to append redacted entries only.

title: Step 1 uses "$D" without defining it or removing it
detail: Step 1 writes the range to "$D" but nothing in CHECKPOINT 0 creates D; run as written the redirect fails and the category falls back; it also never deletes the temp file.
fix_hint: Define and clean up the temp file in the step with the same mktemp guard, trap and subshell pattern as the Phase 1 block.

title: Relay 'go' path is ambiguous about the main re-check and which push remains
detail: After an explicit go it is unclear whether the lead still runs the main push-gate check (and stops on a deny there) and, when the ask was on main's re-check, that only the main push remains; the summary line does not name the ref.
fix_hint: Say the lead still runs the main check and stops on a deny, ignoring only an ask; have the agent's line name the ref ('not pushed (branch|main) — gate asks: …').

title: diff-range exit 2 is described only as 'a refused repository'
detail: In diff-range.js exit 2 also means a range over 32 MiB or a refused driver name; the steps call every exit 2 a refused repository.
fix_hint: Word it as 'Exit 2 is a refusal (a refused repository or driver, or a range over 32 MiB): report the reason as printed'.

title: Step 1 kit-missing branch points to a fallback 'below' that is above
detail: The no-kit branch prints 'use the fallback below' but the git diff fallback is in Step 1's prose before the block, and no scoring is given for the fallback path.
fix_hint: Change the message to 'use the git diff fallback in Step 1's text' or move the fallback sentence after the block.

title: 'a range over 32 MiB' is exit 2 only up to 64 MiB
detail: diff-range exits 2 over graph's maxDiffBytes (32 MiB) but defaultGit reads git stdout with maxBuffer 64 MiB and an overflow is KitExit 1, so a range over 64 MiB is exit 1.
fix_hint: Say 'a range over 32 MiB (exit 1 when git's output passes 64 MiB)' or leave the size out of the exit-2 list.

title: Category scoring counts '+++ <path>' header lines as added content
detail: The greps match ^[+].* and diff-range runs with --no-prefix, so each file's +++ path header is scored; a path holding auth, token, module, cache or error adds points whatever the change.
fix_hint: Exclude headers, e.g. '^[+]([^+]|$).*(…)' or grep -v '^+++ ' before counting.

title: Lead's relay re-check uses $MB, but nothing hands MB to the lead
detail: CHECKPOINT 4 has the lead run push-gate check --base "$MB" after the go, but MB lives only in the background agent and on a branch stop was never recorded, so the lead always runs with an empty MB.
fix_hint: Say the lead records MB itself (Phase 3's record line) before pushing the branch on a branch stop, and have the agent's summary carry MB=<sha> for a main stop.

title: Step 1 real-kit test accepts either of two categories and skips diff-range failure paths
detail: The fixture scores bug 4 against security 3 but the test asserts /CATEGORY=(security|bug)/; it never runs Step 1's diff-range exit 1 or exit 2 branches.
fix_hint: Assert CATEGORY=bug; add a case that makes diff-range fail (include.path in .git/config for exit 2) and assert the stderr message plus CATEGORY=feature.

title: Phase 1 analyses only the redact block's stdout, which carries the whole range as one JSON line and gets cut off on ordinary session sizes
detail: The redact block prints all of redact --keep-lines output to stdout: one JSON object holding a range of up to 32 MiB with escaped newlines. A Bash tool result is capped at about 30K characters, so on any diff over a few tens of KB the only source Analyze may use is truncated; RC-D/RC-F and the solution doc are written from a partial view and the context fills with escaped diff text.
fix_hint: Write redact's text field to a second mktemp file under the same trap and print only replaced, the byte count and the path; Analyze reads that file in chunks or per file; the block deletes it at the end of Phase 1.

title: Step 1 scoring reads the whole range ten times
detail: Five separate grep -v | grep -ciE pipelines make 10 full passes over a temp file of up to 32 MiB.
fix_hint: Compute the five counts in one pass (awk, or one filtered pass into a smaller file), same patterns and weights.

title: mktemp guard can delete files named by inherited J or R
detail: When an earlier mktemp fails the later assignments never run, J and R keep inherited values and the guard's rm -f deletes those files. Reproduced with a missing TMPDIR and an exported R=<file>.
fix_hint: Clear the variables before the guard (D=; J=; R=; ...), or remove only the variables whose mktemp ran.

title: End-of-Phase-1 cleanup of R does nothing as written; the Phase 4 claim is not implemented
detail: R exists only inside the block's subshell; later Bash calls start fresh, so rm -f "$R" and grep/sed "$R" run with R empty and the redacted copy stays in TMPDIR after every successful run. Phase 4 has no line naming it, and the summary is written by the agent, not the lead.
fix_hint: Tell the agent to use the path from the summary's file= field, and add to Phase 4 a line naming that path when it still exists.

title: Prose still quotes the old trap
detail: The paragraph after the block quotes trap 'rm -f "$D"' but the block now sets the D/J/KEEP/R trap.
fix_hint: Quote the current trap line in the prose.

title: Test title claims failure paths leave no file but runs none
detail: The exit-3 case checks only that stdout has no file=; no failure path (redact exit 1, non-JSON output) is run against an empty TMPDIR, so the KEEP-gated removal of R is untested on those paths (a by-hand run shows it is right today).
fix_hint: Run the exit-3 case and one failure case against a fresh empty TMPDIR and assert the dir is empty afterwards.

title: New JSON-to-file step fails with only a Node stack trace
detail: When redact exits 0 but the node -e extraction fails (bad JSON, missing text, write error) the block exits 1 with only Node's stack trace and no line of its own; the prose does not name this path.
fix_hint: Add || echo "redact output could not be written (exit $RC): nothing redacted" >&2 after the node -e step and name the path in the prose.

title: impact runs against the main checkout, not the stream worktree
detail: The impact block takes its diff from diff-range --dir "$W" but calls impact without --dir, so impact resolves dir from the cwd (the main checkout, another branch) and builds the symbol graph from the wrong files; confirmed: 1 touched symbol from the main checkout vs 6 from the worktree, both exit 0 with unmapped empty, so the reviewer gets a wrong blast radius with no sign of it.
fix_hint: Pass --dir "$W" to impact (impact.js accepts it) or run both verbs from inside the worktree with cd "$W"; fix the prose and add a test asserting it.

title: scrub and push-gate check in the worktree never see the private scrub patterns
detail: scrub.js loads .claude/kit/scrub-patterns.local from the working tree's top and the kit install git-ignores that file, so a fresh git worktree add has no copy. With only the private file, scrub reports configured:false with exit 0 and push-gate's scrub block is skipped, so a secret matching a private pattern passes both 4.8 and the pre-push check.
fix_hint: Copy or symlink .claude/kit/scrub-patterns.local into the worktree at 4.2 and check it exists in $W before scanning; treat configured:false in $W as a failure when the main checkout has a pattern file.

title: Streams share one receipt slot, so every earlier stream is blocked at /bcp
detail: push-gate keeps one store file per git common dir, shared by all worktrees, holding a single latest receipt. When the next stream records its receipt, the earlier stream's change id moves to previous and its CHECKPOINT 6 check returns ask 'only an earlier review exists', which the template sorts under 'any other ask' and does not push. A /bc commit in the worktree after the receipt causes the same block.
fix_hint: At CHECKPOINT 6 re-record the stream's receipt from its final review counts after /bc and just before the check; say an 'earlier version' ask can come from another stream's receipt.

title: lenses and impact use the main checkout's kit; receipt, scrub and check use the worktree's
detail: The 4.5 blocks test and run .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js relative to the cwd while every other block uses $W's copy; the copies can differ (here the main checkout has no diff-range verb) and project lenses under .claude/kit/lenses are read from the wrong tree.
fix_hint: Use one kit location for all blocks: run the 4.5 blocks with cd "$W" as the others do.

title: Reading the base with cli.js stream <name> writes to the store
detail: verbStream always calls setStream and refresh; a misspelled name silently creates a new stream row with no base, and BASE comes back empty.
fix_hint: Read the base from a read-only output (cli.js status or streams.json), or warn that the name must match an existing stream exactly.

title: Kit-wiring tests only regex-match text, never run a block
detail: No test runs a block against a real repo with a worktree, which is why the impact/--dir mismatch and the missing private patterns pass the suite.
fix_hint: Add one test that extracts the 4.5 blocks and runs them in a temp repo with a worktree (empty range → exit 0 'no change to review'; a range with changes → lenses/impact output whose root is the worktree).

title: A missing or mistyped worktree is reported as 'kit not installed' and the push gate is skipped
detail: The CHECKPOINT 6 block and both 4.5 receipt blocks test [ ! -f "$W/.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js" ] before entering $W, so a missing or wrong W prints the advisory skip and exits 0, and the lead goes on to /bcp with no receipt, check or scrub. Confirmed with W set to a missing folder.
fix_hint: Enter the worktree before testing for the kit (cd "$W" || { echo "cannot enter the stream worktree $W: not pushed" >&2; exit 1; }) in the CHECKPOINT 6 block and both receipt blocks.

title: The 4.8 check for missing scrub patterns misses the usual case: public file committed, private file missing
detail: The 4.8 guard only fails on configured: false; configured is true when either pattern file exists, and the public file is committed, so a missing .local copy still scans with no private pattern, exits 0 and the stream can close.
fix_hint: In 4.8, before the scrub, loop over both pattern files: if "$M/$P" exists and "$P" does not, print 'scrub patterns missing from the worktree' and exit 2, as CHECKPOINT 6 does.

title: A scrub exit 1 (nothing scanned) still lets the stream close
detail: At 4.8 a scrub exit 1 (bad base, git failure, unreadable pattern file, incomplete history) is reported and the gate still runs, so state=done can follow although the history was never scanned.
fix_hint: Say that a scrub exit 1, or any other non-zero exit, also keeps the stream open until a scrub exits 0.

title: The kit is judged missing from the worktree alone, so a kit the main checkout has but the branch lacks is skipped silently
detail: Every block decides 'kit not installed: advisory' from $W alone; a kit installed but uncommitted in the main checkout makes every worktree skip all five wired steps.
fix_hint: Report 'kit not installed' only when $M/.claude/helpers/kit/cli.js is also missing; otherwise print 'kit missing from the worktree: commit it or copy it' and exit non-zero.

title: The base reader's exit 1 always points at the stream name, even when the file is missing or corrupt
detail: The node -e reader exits 1 with an uncaught stack trace when streams.json is missing or invalid, but the prose says exit 1 means an unknown name or no base.
fix_hint: Wrap the read in try/catch and print 'cannot read <f>: <message>'; add 'or the run folder or streams.json is wrong' to the prose.

title: The CHECKPOINT 6 block does not stop on an empty BASE, and push-gate accepts it without a word
detail: push-gate parses --base "" as empty and falls back to the upstream merge base, so an empty BASE records a receipt and checks a range other than the stream's with no error.
fix_hint: Add [ -n "$BASE" ] || { echo "BASE is empty: read it from streams.json first: not pushed" >&2; exit 1; } at the top of the CHECKPOINT 6 block and the receipt blocks.

title: Folder isolation mode leaves W undefined, and an empty W is never refused
detail: In streams.isolation: folder mode the stream row has no isolation field and the blocks never say what W is. cd "" returns 0, so every block runs silently in the current directory with exit 0, contradicting the 'cannot enter the stream worktree' prose; the 4.2 copy with an empty W writes the private patterns to /.claude/kit when run as root.
fix_hint: Open every block, including the 4.2 copy, with [ -n "$W" ] || { echo "W is empty: set it to the stream's isolation path" >&2; exit 1; }; add a sentence for folder mode: no isolation path, the stream builds in the main checkout, so W=. and the 4.2 copy is skipped.

title: No timeout remedy on slow machines for scrub, diff-range and push-gate check
detail: Each git call stops after 60 s by default; scrub and diff-range exit 1 ('took longer than … raise it with --timeout <ms>'), push-gate check turns a scrub timeout into a deny; the blocks pass no --timeout and 4.8 keeps the stream open until a scrub exits 0. impact has no --timeout flag (its safe-git timeout surfaces as exit 3).
fix_hint: Add one sentence: a 'took longer than … ms' failure is cured by rerunning the same block with --timeout <ms> on scrub, diff-range or push-gate check; impact cannot be raised, report it as a failed step.

title: 4.2 copy creates a missing W and writes the private scrub patterns outside the repo
detail: The guard refuses only an empty W. A non-empty W that does not exist (typo, wrong cwd, a failed git worktree add) makes mkdir -p create the whole path and cp write the private patterns into a stray folder outside the repository; the block exits 0 and the stray folder passes the isDir check of cli.js stream isolation=<path>.
fix_hint: Before the copy: [ -d "$W" ] && git -C "$W" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$W is not the stream worktree: create it first" >&2; exit 1; }; mkdir -p only the .claude/kit subfolder. Add a test with a missing W asserting exit 1 and nothing created.

title: push-gate check cannot exit 1 on a timeout; the remedy sits under the wrong exit
detail: push-gate check builds its own git without a timeout, so it never raises its own 'took longer than' exit 1; --timeout only reaches the scrub, whose timeout becomes a deny (exit 2). The remedy is listed under exit 1.
fix_hint: Move the remedy to the exit-2 bullet: a deny whose reason says the scrub took longer than … ms is cured by rerunning with --timeout <ms> on push-gate check; drop the exit-1 timeout claim.

title: Folder isolation mode: 4.2 and 4.5 now give contradictory instructions
detail: 4.5 says folder mode has no isolation path, W=. and the 4.2 copy is skipped; 4.2 still says to create a folder, copy the private patterns into it and activate with isolation=<path>; the kit's own folder-mode hint is state=active --no-isolation, and the new worktree check refuses a plain folder.
fix_hint: In 4.2 replace '(or a folder when streams.isolation: folder)' with: in folder mode skip 4.2 entirely, activate with cli.js stream <name> state=active --no-isolation and use W=. in every later block.

title: 4.2 copy block never says what W is; its error points to a field not set yet
detail: The block starts with W=../myrepo-api; nothing in 4.2 says to set W to the path given to git worktree add, and the guard message refers to the isolation field that is recorded only after the copy.
fix_hint: Add to 4.2: 'Set W to the path you gave git worktree add', and make the 4.2 guard say 'set it to the new worktree path'.

title: CHECKPOINT 6 timeout remedy quotes text the deny reason does not contain
detail: push-gate's scrubBlock prints 'the scrub check is configured but could not run: git <cmd> took longer than N ms and was stopped (raise it with --timeout <ms>)'; the phrase 'the scrub took longer' never appears.
fix_hint: Quote the real wording.

title: Stale quote of the 4.2 copy's empty-W message
detail: 4.5 still quotes the copy block's empty-W message as 'set it to the stream's isolation path' while round 5 changed the 4.2 copy to print 'set it to the new worktree path'. Behaviour unaffected; the two sections disagree on the quoted text.
fix_hint: Say the 4.2 copy prints 'new worktree path' and the kit blocks print 'the stream's isolation path', or drop 'the 4.2 copy included' from the quoted clause; regenerate.

title: Wired text lists `blame` as a safe-git read, but safe-git refuses blame (exit 2)
detail: CHECKPOINT 4 step 2 (and SAFE_GIT_LINES in src/lib/bbs/inventory.js:492 and src/lib/bbs/harness-map.js:511, with their .claude/helpers/bbs copies and src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:4374) says every git read 'log, show, ls-files, blame, cat-file' goes through safe-git. safe-git.js READ_SUBCOMMANDS (line 156) does not include blame, and its header (line 82) names blame as refused. A probe helper that follows the text and runs `safe-git ... -- blame` gets exit 2, and the same step tells it to 'return `incomplete`' on exit 2, which removes `use` from that power's verdict. The workflow text says the verb does something its code refuses, and on that path the probe result comes out wrong.
fix_hint: Drop blame from the list, or name the allowed subcommands (log, show, ls-files, ls-tree, cat-file, diff, rev-list) in all three places. Add a test asserting every subcommand named in the text is in safe-git's READ_SUBCOMMANDS.

title: CHECKPOINT 6 runs `git add -A` over the whole worktree before /bc, against /bc's own staging rule
detail: The block stages every modified and untracked file in the user's project (`git add -A -- . ':!fetched'`), including unrelated work in progress. /bc (w-background-compound.md:108,149) says to stage only the paths it wrote ('NOT git add -A') and to commit with `git commit -- <paths>`. As a result, unrelated user files stay staged after the run. scrub exit 2 can also flag unrelated files and block /bc. If scrub fails, the user's index has already been changed and nothing undoes it. /bc already stages its own paths and scrubs them before committing, so this pre-step widens the scope instead of adding coverage.
fix_hint: Stage only the run's own paths, e.g. `git add -- .claude/bbs/runs/<id>` plus the registry/labels files the run wrote. Alternatively, drop the bbs-level `git add` and rely on /bc's scoped stage-then-scrub.

title: Pathspec `:!fetched` does not exclude the real fetched/ folder, and the test pins that wording
detail: fetched/ lives at .claude/bbs/runs/<id>/fetched/ (fetch.js:606). The exclude pathspec `:!fetched`, relative to the project root, only matches a top-level `fetched`. The only thing keeping the clone out is the .gitignore rule `.claude/bbs/runs/*/fetched/`. The text reads as if the pathspec does the exclusion, and the test asserts that pathspec verbatim.
fix_hint: Use `':(exclude,glob).claude/bbs/runs/*/fetched/**'` (or stage only run paths, per the medium finding) and assert that in the test.

title: Text says `replaced` in the JSON counts replacements, but the block never shows the JSON
detail: The redact block writes the JSON to $J, prints only `.text`, and the EXIT trap deletes $J. The lead never sees `replaced`, so the sentence 'Exit 0: redacted (`replaced` in the JSON counts the replacements)' points at output that is never printed.
fix_hint: Also print `replaced` to stderr from the node one-liner, or drop the parenthetical.

title: Inventory brief adds the git/clone section for every source type, including page/URL sources with no clone
detail: inventoryBrief receives `source` (type page/url/repo) but always pushes SAFE_GIT_LINES. For a fetched page (fetched/1.html) there is no clone and no `<clone top>`, so the helper gets instructions that do not apply to its input.
fix_hint: Push SAFE_GIT_LINES only when the source is a cloned repository (source.type for git, or files.root ending in fetched/repo).

title: SAFE_GIT_LINES duplicated verbatim in two modules
detail: The same nine-line constant is defined in inventory.js:490 and harness-map.js:509 (and in both .claude/helpers/bbs copies). Any wording fix, such as the blame correction, has to be made in four places, and the copies can drift.
fix_hint: Export it once (e.g. from inventory.js or a small shared module) and import it in harness-map.js.

title: Secrets pre-check reads a broken secrets file as 'nothing to redact'
detail: The CHECKPOINT 4 block uses `[ ! -f .claude/kit/secrets ]` to short-circuit before redact. `-f` is false for a dangling symlink or a directory at that path, so the block prints 'no .claude/kit/secrets: evidence recorded as is, nothing to redact' and exits 0. In those cases redact itself exits 1: readFileOr treats a dangling symlink as broken, not absent, and a directory gives EISDIR. Verified in a scratch repo. Dangling symlink: block rc=0 'nothing to redact', direct `redact` rc=1 'cannot read secrets file ... ENOENT'. Directory: block rc=0, direct rc=1 EISDIR. A broken state that the verb reports as exit 1 is turned into a clean 'nothing to redact', which the run's rules forbid. The text right below says 'never read exit 1 as nothing to redact'. The test at test/w-bbs-command.test.js:291 pins this wording.
fix_hint: Drop the secrets pre-check (redact already returns replaced=0 when the default file is truly absent), or test with `-e`/`-L` instead of `-f` so anything present at the path goes to redact and its exit 1 surfaces. Adjust the test assertion to match.

title: Refused scrub leaves the run's paths staged, with the hit in the index
detail: CHECKPOINT 6 runs `git add -- .claude/bbs/runs/<id>` (and the registry) before `scrub --worktree`. On exit 2 with hits in those paths, it only says not to run /bc until the hits are removed. It never unstages, and it never says to re-add after the fix. scrub --worktree reads files on disk, so after the user edits out a hit, a re-scan is clean while the index still holds the staged blob with the secret. A plain `git commit` by the user, or a stop at this point, keeps that secret-bearing blob in the index. /bc's own refused-scrub path does unstage (`git reset -q -- <paths>`, w-background-compound.md:107), so the two disagree on the same error path.
fix_hint: On any non-zero scrub exit (and on a failed git add), run `git reset -q -- .claude/bbs/runs/<id> .claude/bbs/registry.jsonl` and check its exit, as /bc does. Or say the paths must be re-added after the hits are removed and before the re-scan.

title: Redacted evidence from untrusted source is pasted into a double-quoted shell argument
detail: The new redact step keeps the evidence in a file ($E, then $J), prints the redacted `text`, then says 'Use the printed text as the evidence ... verdict --probe ... --evidence "<text>"'. This evidence quotes the fetched, untrusted source, and probes hunt for network calls, so it often holds JS template literals such as fetch(`${BASE}/t`). Inside double quotes, backticks and $( ) run as commands and ${X} expands, which corrupts the record and executes text derived from the clone. The shape predates this diff, but the diff rewrote this line and already had the evidence in a file, where a safe hand-off costs nothing.
fix_hint: Write the redacted text to a file $R inside the block and record it with `--evidence "$(cat "$R")"` (command-substitution output is not re-evaluated), or add an --evidence-file flag.

title: Scrub exit 2 gate looks only at hits, not at an incomplete or truncated scan of the run's paths
detail: The text says exit 2 blocks /bc only for 'hits in this run's paths', and hits elsewhere are left alone. Exit 2 also means complete:false (files in not_scanned: a tracked file missing on disk, a file over --max-file-bytes) or truncated:true (1000-hit cap). Suppose a run-path file is in not_scanned, or pre-existing hits elsewhere fill the cap. Then no run-path hit is shown, the gate's condition is met vacuously, and /bc proceeds over an unscanned run file. That is a non-zero exit read as clean for the run.
fix_hint: Add: if `complete` is false for any run path, or `truncated` is true, treat it as a block (or re-run after cleaning) rather than as 'no hits in run paths'.

title: SAFE_GIT_LINES says safe-git always prints the JSON object; on exit 1/2 it prints nothing on stdout
detail: The brief tells helpers 'It prints { stdout, stderr, code, exit }. Read the exit: ...'. Verified in a scratch repo that this JSON is printed only for exit 0 and 3. For exit 1 (e.g. --dir is a subfolder) and exit 2 (e.g. blame/push refused), stdout is empty and the reason is a `kit:` / `kit: refused:` line on stderr. A helper that parses stdout for the JSON gets a parse error instead of the refusal reason it is told to name in evidence. The same wording appears in the CHECKPOINT 4 probe instruction (w-bbs.md line 124).
fix_hint: Say: exit 0/3 print { stdout, stderr, code, exit }; exit 1/2 print only a `kit:` line on stderr. Read the process exit code, not a field.

title: safe-git exit 3 from a timeout prints no JSON, but the wired text says exit 3 always prints it
detail: CP4 step 2 says '3 git failed or timed out (it prints `{ stdout, stderr, code, exit }`)' and 'only exits 0 and 3 print that JSON'. SAFE_GIT_LINES (src/lib/bbs/inventory.js:494, mirrored in .claude/helpers/bbs/inventory.js) says the same. In safe-git.js:272-275, defaultGitRunner throws KitExit(..., 3) on ETIMEDOUT, ENOBUFS (output over 256 MiB) and a signal kill. cli.js turns that into a `kit: ...` line on stderr with nothing on stdout. Reproduced: `safe-git --timeout 1 --dir <clone> -- log` gives stdout empty, stderr 'kit: git config took longer than 1 ms and was stopped (raise it with --timeout <ms>)', rc=3. On slow disks, network filesystems or very large clones the 60 s default timeout is the realistic exit-3 path. Neither text mentions --timeout.
fix_hint: Say exit 3 prints the JSON when git ran and failed, and only a `kit:` stderr line when git timed out, overflowed or was killed. Note that `--timeout <ms>` raises the 60000 ms default. Apply the same wording in CP4 and SAFE_GIT_LINES (both copies).

title: CP6 does not cover scrub exit 2 as a refusal (no JSON, nothing scanned), so the lead can read it as 'no run-path hits'
detail: scrub reports safe-git refusals (KitExit 2) as exit 2 with only a `kit: refused:` line on stderr and no JSON. That happens when the user's own project uses object alternates (a `git clone --shared` or `--reference` clone), has more than 100000 loose objects, has .git on a network path, or has more than 200000 tracked files. Reproduced in a `--shared` clone with a real hit in .claude/bbs/runs/r1/labels.jsonl: rc=2, 'kit: refused: ... borrows objects from ...', no hits list. The CP6 text treats exit 2 only as 'hits or an incomplete scan' and blocks /bc only on run-path hits, `complete: false` with run paths in not_scanned, or `truncated: true`. On a refusal none of these fields exists, so a literal reading finds no run-path hits and proceeds to /bc. A refusal also cannot be cleared by removing hits.
fix_hint: Add: exit 2 with no JSON and a `kit: refused:` line on stderr means nothing was scanned. Report the reason verbatim. It is not clean and is never read as 'no hits in this run's paths'. Treat it like exit 1 (advisory: the lead sees the reason before /bc), or block /bc. Do not tell the lead to remove hits.

title: Recording with `"$(cat "$R")"` silently records empty evidence when $R or $E is not set in that shell
detail: The block prints `file=<path>` and the text says 'call it `$R`'. The record command is then given literally as `--evidence "$(cat "$R")"`, followed by `rm -f "$R" "$E"`. Shell variables do not persist between the agent's separate Bash calls, and the block's own `$E` must also be set in the same command, which the text never shows. If the lead runs the record command as printed, `cat ''` fails on stderr and the substitution is empty. The command becomes `--evidence ''`; sanitizeEvidence returns null, and verdict exits 0 with no evidence and no error. Verified: with R unset, argc=2 and the evidence argument is ''. The probe's reason is lost with no non-zero exit to catch it.
fix_hint: Show the variables bound in the same command, e.g. `E=<path>; <block>` and `R=<printed path>; [ -s "$R" ] || { echo 'evidence file missing or empty' >&2; exit 1; }; node .../cli.js verdict --probe ... --evidence "$(cat -- "$R")"`. Or tell the lead to write the literal printed path in place of $R and $E.

title: Test pins the incorrect wording 'only exits 0 and 3 print that JSON'
detail: Lines 262 and 265 assert the exact sentences that claim exit 3 always prints `{ stdout, stderr, code, exit }`. safe-git's timeout, overflow and signal paths print no JSON, so the test locks in a false claim and will resist the fix.
fix_hint: Assert the corrected wording: JSON on 0 and on a git-ran exit 3, and a `kit:` stderr line on a timeout, overflow or kill. Ideally also add a run-based check that `safe-git --timeout 1` exits 3 with empty stdout.

title: The exit-1 cause lists for scrub and redact leave out git failures, timeouts and a missing git
detail: CP6 calls scrub exit 1 'wrong input or a broken state'. scrub's usage and scrub.js:39-43 say exit 1 is also 'git failed/timed out' (default 60 s), the likely cause on slow or old machines, and no --timeout hint is given. The CP4 redact list ('unreadable secrets file, dangling symlink, directory, bad flag, mktemp failed') leaves out 'cannot run git' (git not installed) and 'not inside a git repository / git rev-parse failed' (redact.js secretsRoots).
fix_hint: Add 'git failed or timed out (raise with --timeout <ms>)' to the scrub exit-1 sentence. Add 'git missing or not a git repository' to the redact exit-1 list.

title: The probe is pointed at history reads on a depth-1 clone, where any read past HEAD exits 3 and forces 'incomplete'
detail: bbs fetch always clones with `--depth 1 --no-tags` (fetch.js:466). CP4 lists log, diff and rev-list as reads and maps every exit 3 to 'return incomplete', which removes `use`. Reproduced: `safe-git ... -- show HEAD~1` on the shallow clone gives 'unknown revision', rc=3. A clean source then loses `use` because of the clone's missing history, not because of anything in the code.
fix_hint: Say the clone has a single commit (depth 1), so only HEAD and its tree are readable. An exit 3 from asking for history beyond HEAD means the call was wrong (fix it and retry once), not that the source is incomplete.

title: CP6 scrub runs without --json, so a hit in this run's paths can be hidden past the 50 hits shown while truncated stays false
detail: The CP6 block runs `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js scrub --worktree` without `--json`. In scrub.js report(), the non-JSON result shows only `hits.slice(0, LIMITS.shown)` (50) and reports the rest as `hits_not_shown`. `truncated` becomes true only at the 1000-hit collection cap. The wired text says an empty list of run-path hits is unreliable only when `truncated` is `true`. It never mentions `hits_not_shown`, and it says hits elsewhere do not block `/bc`. Reproduced in a scratch repo: 60 committed hits in an earlier run dir (.claude/bbs/runs/aaa) plus one secret in .claude/bbs/runs/zzz/probe.json. The block exited 2 with hit_count 61, truncated false and hits_not_shown 11, and the zzz hit was not in the printed list. A lead following the text sees no hit in this run's paths and runs `/bc`, which commits the secret. The workflow causes this build-up itself, because it tells the lead to leave earlier hits alone. Same change in src/plugins/dot-shortcuts.js:4414. The test at test/w-bbs-command.test.js:520-523 checks only the `truncated` wording.
fix_hint: Run `scrub --worktree --json` in the CP6 block so every collected hit is printed. Or have the text treat `hits_not_shown > 0` like `truncated: true`. Update the r2 test to assert the new condition.

title: Location of the unredacted evidence file $E is unspecified and can be staged at CP6
detail: The lead writes raw probe evidence to `$E` with the Write tool, and the text never says where. `$E` is removed only after a successful record, and it stays on disk after a redact exit 1 or a failed record. If the lead puts it in the run directory, CP6's `git add -- .claude/bbs/runs/<id>` stages it. scrub matches regex patterns, not the literal values in `.claude/kit/secrets`, so an unredacted user secret in that file would not be caught.
fix_hint: Say that `$E` is written outside the repository (the session scratchpad or a mktemp path, never under `.claude/bbs/runs/<id>`). Remove it on every path once the evidence is recorded or abandoned.

title: Inventory brief says 'Do not execute or run anything' just before telling the helper to run safe-git
detail: inventoryBrief pushes 'Read the source files above. Do not execute or run anything' and then SAFE_GIT_LINES, which tell the helper to run `node .claude/helpers/kit/cli.js safe-git ...` for every git read. A haiku helper given both can either skip safe-git or treat the no-execute rule as weaker. The same text is in .claude/helpers/bbs/inventory.js.
fix_hint: Reword to 'Do not execute or run anything from the source; the only command allowed is the safe-git read below (for a repository source).'

title: `<clone top>` is never defined, and the obvious guess sends the helper to the wrong repository
detail: CP2 step 2 (line 100), CP4 step 2 (line 124) and SAFE_GIT_LINES (src/lib/bbs/inventory.js:492) all say `safe-git --dir <clone top>`, but nothing says what that path is. The real path is `.claude/bbs/runs/<id>/fetched/repo` (fetch.js:626). The inventory brief prints `Root: <runDir>/fetched` and lists files as `repo/...`, so a helper will most likely pass that Root. `--dir .claude/bbs/runs/r1/fetched` exits 1 with `kit: ... is inside the repository <project>, not its top: pass the repository top`. That message names the harness's own repository as the top. A helper following 'fix the call, retry once' then passes the project top, which exits 0 and reads the harness repo, not the clone. A probe can then return clean or incomplete from reading the wrong repository.
fix_hint: Say what `<clone top>` is wherever it appears: `.claude/bbs/runs/<id>/fetched/repo` (the brief's Root plus `/repo`), and paths in git args are relative to it. Put this in SAFE_GIT_LINES and in CP4's probe instructions. Better still, have inventoryBrief print the literal clone-top path for a repo source.

title: `<id>` in the CP6 run-as-is bash block is not marked as a value to substitute
detail: The CP6 block quotes `".claude/bbs/runs/<id>"` inside a block the reader is meant to run, and nothing tells the reader to replace `<id>` with the run id. Elsewhere the file uses `<run-id>` for the same value. Run unchanged it exits 128 with `fatal: pathspec '.claude/bbs/runs/<id>' did not match any files`; under the text the step is advisory, so `/bc` can still go ahead.
fix_hint: Add one sentence before the block: 'Replace every `<id>` in the block with this run's id (the `<run-id>` from intake) before running it.'

title: Probe exit-3 rule reads as 'return incomplete', then is partly reversed later; the brief says something different
detail: In CP4 the exit-3 entry ends with ': return `incomplete`'. The depth-1 exception only comes two sentences later. That rule also covers ordinary git-ran failures such as `show HEAD:<missing path>`, so a typo in a path marks the whole source incomplete and removes `use`. SAFE_GIT_LINES says only '3 git itself failed or timed out: say so', so the two texts disagree on the same exit code.
fix_hint: Put all exit-3 handling in one place: a timeout, overflow or kill returns incomplete; git ran and failed on a wrong call (a missing path, history beyond HEAD) means fix it and retry once. Use the same wording in the workflow text and SAFE_GIT_LINES.

title: CP2 tells every inventory helper to use safe-git '(the brief says so)', but for non-repo sources the brief forbids every command
detail: CP2 step 2 tells each helper, whatever the source type, that git reads of the clone go through safe-git, and adds 'the brief says so'. For url, local and paste sources, inventoryBrief says 'run no command at all' and leaves out SAFE_GIT_LINES. So the parenthetical is false for those sources, and the helper gets two conflicting instructions.
fix_hint: Limit the sentence to repository sources: 'For a repository source, tell each helper ... (the brief says so)'.

title: SAFE_GIT_LINES tells the inventory helper to 'return `incomplete`', but the inventory JSON shape has no such value
detail: SAFE_GIT_LINES is printed only in the inventory helper brief (repo sources). Round 5 added: 'Exit 3 is handled one way: a timeout, overflow or kill ... returns `incomplete`; ... only a second failure on a correct call returns `incomplete`.' `clean|found|incomplete` is the CP4 probe helper's verdict. The inventory helper returns `{ powers: [...] }` or `{ powers: [], none_found }`. In a scratch run, `inventory --from` rejected `{"incomplete":"..."}` with exit 1 ('input must have a "powers" field'), and `{"powers":[],"incomplete":"x"}` with exit 1. An inventory helper that follows its brief on a safe-git timeout returns a shape the CLI refuses, or drops the source's powers without saying why. The same sentence is pinned for SAFE_GIT_LINES by the r5 test (the `for (const t of [s, g])` loop), and .claude/helpers/bbs/inventory.js carries the same text.
fix_hint: In SAFE_GIT_LINES, replace 'returns `incomplete`' with an instruction the inventory schema can carry, e.g. 'stop reading that file and name the failed read (the kit: line) in the evidence of the affected power, or in none_found'. Keep the `incomplete` wording in CP4 only, and split the test so SAFE_GIT_LINES asserts the inventory-shaped instruction.

title: Brief says the Clone top it prints is `.claude/bbs/runs/<run-id>/fetched/repo`, but it prints an absolute path, and its file list is prefixed `repo/`
detail: resolveProjectDir returns an absolute path, so the real brief prints 'Root: /abs/.../fetched' and 'Clone top (for safe-git --dir): /abs/.../fetched/repo'. SAFE_GIT_LINES, CP2 and CP4 call it the relative `.claude/bbs/runs/<run-id>/fetched/repo`. The 'Files in this source' list names files relative to Root (`repo/a.js`), while git args must be relative to the clone top. A helper that copies a listed path (`show HEAD:repo/a.js`) gets exit 3 with 'path does not exist', and nothing tells it to drop the `repo/` prefix. Both forms of --dir work, so this misleads mildly; the r5 test only covers a relative root.
fix_hint: Say 'the Clone top line (the absolute path of .claude/bbs/runs/<run-id>/fetched/repo)', and add to SAFE_GIT_LINES: 'listed files start with `repo/`; drop that prefix in git args'.

title: Range description leaves out the no-upstream case, where removal detection is always empty
detail: Every wired Code Analysis step (lines 409, 1175, 1851, 2151, 2646 and 5620) says the range is 'everything since the merge base with the upstream branch'. When there is no upstream, diff-range falls back to the empty tree. That is the usual state of a local feature or hotfix branch before the first push. Then lenses and impact cover the whole repository, and impact's removed_with_live_callers is always [], because nothing is 'removed' relative to the empty tree. Checked in a scratch repo: removing an exported f that b.js still calls gave removed_with_live_callers=[] with no upstream, and one entry once an upstream existed. The text tells the reader to treat that list as the defect signal, so an empty list reads as 'no broken callers'. w-review.md already says '(the whole history when there is no upstream)'.
fix_hint: Add the w-review wording to the shared sentence: '(the whole history when there is no upstream: then removed_with_live_callers cannot find removals, so say the removal check did not run)'.

title: w-end: on a scrub refusal the gate still says 'Commit complete' and offers 'Push to remote'
detail: The new Checkpoint 2 text says that after a scrub refusal nothing is committed and the paths are unstaged. The USER GATE right after it is unchanged on every path: 'Commit complete. Session ended.' with options ["Done", "Push to remote"]. On the refusal path this tells the user a commit happened and offers a push. The push path also runs no push-gate check. Judgment call (b): leaving out the receipt in w-end, w-autoresearch and w-ralph-pick is acceptable, because the gate then asks 'no review recorded' and the push goes on. The problem is the push offer itself: it is unconditional and runs no check.
fix_hint: Make the gate conditional: after a refusal ask 'Not committed: scrub refused. Fix and retry?' with no push option. On 'Push to remote', run the guarded push-gate check block from w-agent-tdd-swarm step 5 first.

title: 'add its findings to the review output below' points the wrong way, or to nothing
detail: In w-tdd-swarm, w-debug, w-security and w-hotfix the Code Analysis block comes after the review's REQUIRED OUTPUT table (lines 1192, 1868, 2168 and 2663), so 'below' is wrong. In w-ralph-pick (line 5629) there is no review output at all and no receipt, so the lens findings have nowhere to go.
fix_hint: Say 'add its findings to the review findings above'. In w-ralph-pick, add a 'Lens findings: _____' line to that checkpoint's REQUIRED OUTPUT.

title: w-agent-tdd-swarm: a failed receipt leads to a push labelled 'no review recorded'
detail: If step 4 (receipt) exits 1 or 2, the text only says to report it. Step 5's check then asks 'no review recorded for this change', the push goes on, and the summary says 'no review recorded'. A review did run, but its receipt was not written. Step 4 also does not say which verdict to record when only medium or low findings remain, and does not name 'any other non-zero exit'.
fix_hint: In step 4, say a failed receipt means 'not pushed: receipt not recorded (exit N)'. Name any other non-zero exit. Give the rule: verdict fail when any high finding is open, else pass.

title: Regeneration brings a Pi Brain curl block with an unbalanced quote into four copies
detail: Regenerating adds the Pi Brain checkpoint to w-agent-tdd-swarm, w-tdd-swarm, w-debug and w-hotfix (generator lines 307 and 1088, among others). Its first curl line, "https://pi.ruv.io/v1/memories/search "[feature description]" --top-k=3, leaves a quote open: bash -n fails with 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching "'. The line is commented as an 'npm client' although it is a curl call. Pre-existing in the generator, but this diff puts it in these copies.
fix_hint: Fix the generator line, for example: curl -s -G "https://pi.ruv.io/v1/memories/search" --data-urlencode "q=[feature description]" --data top_k=3. Or drop the broken 'npm client' line.

title: Regenerated w-end drops 'AUTO-PROCEED: Continue to Commit phase.'
detail: The old copy ended Checkpoint 1 with '**AUTO-PROCEED:** Continue to Commit phase.'. The generator has no such line, so the regenerated copy lost it, while the completion checklist still says 'Checkpoint 1 completed (auto-proceed)'. The same regeneration also moved the Verification checkpoint in w-hotfix and removed the agent-browser lines in w-security. Judgment call (a): the restored RuFlo blocks match the old copies byte for byte.
fix_hint: Restore the AUTO-PROCEED line in the generator's w-end entry after the Ralph candidate check, then regenerate.
